---
title: "Data Infrastructure"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "The engines that get your data in and shape it: Airhouse, Airway, and Airform"
---

Data Infrastructure is the foundation of Oxygen, getting your data in and
shaping it into clean tables that your [World Model](/guide/build/world-model)
and agents can query. Three engines do the work:

- **Airway** *loads*: it extracts data from the systems you already run and
  loads it into your warehouse, picking up where the last run left off.
- **Airhouse** *stores*: it is the managed, Postgres-compatible warehouse
  where that data lands, with short-lived credentials and no key to rotate.
- **Airform** *shapes*: it turns raw tables into clean, tested ones with
  dbt-style SQL models that live in your workspace.

## One workspace, from source to model

A typical data stack is stitched together from separate products: an ELT
service to move data, a warehouse to hold it, a transformation tool to model
it, and a semantic layer on top. Each has its own configuration, its own
credentials, and its own deploy process, and the seams between them are where
numbers drift and failures hide.

In Oxygen, every step lives in one workspace. A pipeline is a `.airway.yml`
file, a model is a `.sql` file, and a measure is defined in a `.view.yml`
file, all reviewed and deployed through the same Git flow as your agents and
automations. A change to how data is loaded, shaped, or measured is a single
pull request, and the tables an agent reads are built from files you can see.

## Load: Airway

[Airway](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airway) pipelines extract data from
point-of-sale platforms, accounting tools, databases, files, public datasets,
and any system with an HTTP API. Each run extracts only what changed since the
last one, and a failed run can be retried without re-pulling history.
Pipelines run on demand, on a schedule, or as a step in an
[automation](/guide/build/automations/task-types#type-airway).

## Store: Airhouse

[Airhouse](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airhouse) is the warehouse where
pipelines land their data and where agents query it. Each workspace gets its
own isolated Airhouse database, served over the Postgres wire protocol, and
access runs on credentials minted on demand rather than on a stored password.
If you already have a warehouse, Oxygen
[connects to your own](/guide/build/connect-data) instead.

## Shape: Airform

[Airform](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airform) compiles a dbt-style
project of SQL models into plain SQL, builds the models in dependency order on
your warehouse, and runs their tests, so the tables downstream are clean and
checked rather than assembled ad hoc.

## Model: the World Model

The [World Model](/guide/build/world-model) builds on the clean tables. Its
[semantic model](/guide/build/semantic-model/simple-model) defines each measure
once and compiles it into correct SQL, so agents and apps answer and act on the
same numbers.
